widgetsPage.addToLayoutHint: Puts the widget on the first monitor of the layout on screen

from-the-future.title: Your settings were saved by a newer version
from-the-future.description: This build cannot read them, and will not overwrite them. Update Marble Trace to get your layouts and bindings back.

too-old.title: Your settings are too old to upgrade automatically
too-old.description: They were saved by a version too far back for this build to convert. The file has been left untouched.

corrupt.title: Your settings file could not be read
corrupt.description: It has been left untouched so it can be recovered by hand. Marble Trace is running on defaults and will not save over it.

settingsLock.lastGoodAvailable: A copy from {{date}}, saved the last time the file loaded cleanly, can be restored.
settingsLock.restoreConfirm: Replace the unreadable file with the copy saved before it broke? The unreadable file is kept beside it.
settingsLock.restoreFailed: The restore failed and nothing was changed. The log has the reason.
settingsLock.restoredRestartRequired: The last good copy is back in place, but Marble Trace could not restart itself. Close it and start it again to load it.
settingsLock.resetConfirm: Replace the settings file with defaults? Layouts, widgets and bindings in it will be lost.

layoutEditor.applyLayoutTooltip: Apply this layout to the overlay
layoutEditor.monitorTooltip: Choose the screen to edit, or view them all at once. Picking a screen the layout does not cover yet adds it.
layoutEditor.viewOverviewTooltip: Every screen of the layout at once
layoutEditor.viewFullSizeTooltip: One screen filling the app window
layoutEditor.viewFullscreenTooltip: One screen filling its real monitor
layoutEditor.addRemoteScreenTooltip: Add a virtual screen — not a monitor of this PC, but a page a browser opens by link: a tablet, a phone, or a browser source in OBS
layoutEditor.arrangeRemoteScreensTooltip: Lay the browser screens out in rows under the desktop, widgets included
layoutEditor.addRemoteScreenHint: Anything that opens the link renders this screen: a tablet on your network, or a Browser Source in OBS. Make the ground transparent for OBS, and size the source to match — the first one that connects reports its own size, and fitting to it moves every widget on the screen.
layoutEditor.remoteScreenReuseHint: Reuses this screen with its URL and dimensions in the current layout.
layoutEditor.quickPlacementDesc: Puts the widget in a corner, an edge or the centre of its screen.
layoutEditor.copySettingsFromDesc: Takes another instance's settings; keeps this one's place and size
layoutEditor.resetSettingsConfirm: Put this widget's settings back to the defaults?
layoutEditor.hotkeysActOnDesc: Its hotkeys show, hide and switch this instance. With several marked, they all change together. A browser screen follows them too, so a stream shows what you switched to.

monitorMap.notInLayout: Not in this layout — click to add
monitorMap.addToLayout: Add this monitor to the layout
monitorMap.identifyTooltip: Show each monitor’s number on the monitor itself
monitorMap.title: Monitor arrangement and browser screens

layoutList.removeMonitorWithWidgets: Remove this monitor and its {{count}} widgets?

autoSwitch.title: Auto-switch
autoSwitch.description: Put a layout on screen when the situation in the sim changes. Each rule names a session, a car class and a car, any of them "any"; the most specific matching rule wins: a car over a class, a class over a session. Layouts are assigned here only.
autoSwitch.noRules: No rules yet. Add one to put a layout on screen by session, car class or car.

layoutList.exportFailed: Could not save the layout file
layoutList.importFailed: This file holds no Marble Trace layout

layoutWidgetPanel.copyTooltip: A copy — its own settings, place and switch
layoutWidgetPanel.originalTooltip: The first instance on this screen; the others here are its copies
layoutWidgetPanel.hotkeysOn: Hotkeys act on this widget — click to exclude it
layoutWidgetPanel.hotkeysOff: Hotkeys skip this widget — click to include it

layoutCanvas.nothingToShow: Nothing to show in this scenario

widgetSettings.fontScaleDesc: Scales only the text, independent of widget width/height
widgetSettings.hotkeysShared: Shared by all copies of this widget

widgetDisplayOverride.title: Widget Display Override
widgetDisplayOverride.hideAllDesc: Global toggle to quickly hide or show all enabled UI elements.

startupBehavior.title: Startup Behavior
startupBehavior.launchMinimizedDesc: Start the application minimized to the taskbar.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.headerAnimationDesc: The calm wave behind the header. Pauses when the window is minimised or not focused.

interactionMode.title: Interaction Mode
interactionMode.dragModeDesc: Unlock widgets to move them freely across the screen.
interactionMode.interactModeDesc: Let the mouse reach the overlay (scrolling, buttons) without unlocking widget dragging. While it is on, the game does not receive the mouse.
interactionMode.interactHotkeyModeDesc: Toggle switches the mode on and off, Hold keeps it on only while the key is pressed.
interactionMode.interactAutoOffDesc: Turn interact mode off automatically so the mouse returns to the game.

gameIntegration.title: Game Integration
gameIntegration.autoHideDesc: Hide widgets when the simulator is not running.

overlayPerformance.title: Performance
overlayPerformance.updateRateDesc: How often widgets redraw. Every redraw costs the game a composited frame: 60 Hz moves smoothest and costs the most dropped frames, 30 Hz keeps motion smooth at a fraction of the cost.

steeringLock.title: Steering Wheel
steeringLock.rangeDesc: Physical range of your wheel: {{full}}° (±{{half}}°). Shared by every widget that shows steering.

pitStrategy.title: Pit stop strategy
pitStrategy.desc: Applies to the one car in the sim, whichever screen shows the pit box.
pitStrategy.autoFuelDesc: Auto mode checks the fuel amount the Fuel widget calculates, capped at tank capacity.
pitStrategy.autoTiresDesc: Auto mode checks the corners worn past the threshold below, one corner at a time.
pitStrategy.autoTireWearThreshold: Change a tire at {{percent}}% tread left
pitStrategy.fuelAdjustStepDesc: How much one press of the fuel up / down keys adds or removes, in the unit you read — litres on metric, gallons on imperial.
pitStrategy.pressureAdjustStepDesc: How much one press of the pressure buttons and keys changes a tyre. Setting a pressure also orders that tyre changed — the sim has no pressure without the change.

fuelStrategy.title: Fuel strategy
fuelStrategy.desc: Applies to the fuel figures of every Fuel widget on every screen — the app works them out once for the car.
fuelStrategy.pitWarningLapsDesc: The Fuel widget warns when this many laps of fuel are left.
fuelStrategy.fuelAvgWindow: Consumption averaging window, laps (0 = all laps)
fuelStrategy.fuelAvgWindowDesc: Nearly the whole widget is derived from this average: the summary AVG cell, LAPS LEFT, the fuel left at the finish, the refuel amount and the pit window edges. A short window tracks the current pace but jumps around; a long one reads steady but is slow to follow a change in pace or weather. The AVG ALL column always spans every lap, so the two read side by side. At 0 the AVG ALL column is hidden — it would repeat the summary cell.
fuelStrategy.countYellowFlagLapsDesc: Use laps run under a local yellow flag in the fuel average. On a road course a yellow rarely slows the lap enough to change consumption. Full-course cautions and red flags are always left out.

carLength.title: Car
carLength.valueDesc: The length of a car in meters. Turns the distance between car centres into the gap between bumpers, so cars nose to tail read zero. Shared by the radars and Close Battle.

applicationUpdates.title: Application Updates
applicationUpdates.autoCheckDesc: Automatically check for new versions on application startup.
applicationUpdates.checkIntervalDesc: How often to check for updates while the app is running.
applicationUpdates.upToDate: Your application is up to date.

about.title: About Marble Trace
about.tagline: A telemetry overlay for iRacing. Free and open source under GPL-3.0.
about.trademarks: Marble Trace™ and the Marble Trace logo are trademarks of voof. iRacing is a trademark of iRacing.com Motorsport Simulations, LLC. TAURI is trademark of The Tauri Programme within the Commons Conservancy. Windows is a trademark of the Microsoft group of companies. Twitch is a trademark of Twitch Interactive, Inc. YouTube is a trademark of Google LLC. All other names are the property of their respective owners.
about.independence: Marble Trace is an independent open-source project. It is not made by iRacing, has no connection to iRacing.com Motorsport Simulations, LLC, and is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by it or by any of the companies below.

trackMap.title: Track Map
trackMap.reRecordDesc: Clears current map data and starts fresh on next lap crossing or manual trigger.
trackMap.manualStartActive: Manual start active. Drive to begin recording.
trackMap.pitLaneCalibrationDescWithTrack: Clears pit entry/exit points recorded for "{{track}}". Drive through the pit lane again to re-calibrate.
trackMap.pitLaneCalibrationDescNoTrack: No track loaded. Load a session to reset pit lane data for the active track.
trackMap.pitLaneResetSuccess: Pit lane data cleared. Drive through pit lane to re-calibrate.
trackMap.referenceLapDescWithCar: Deletes the stored best lap for "{{car}}" on the current track. Recording restarts on the next completed lap.
trackMap.referenceLapDescNoSession: No session loaded. Load a session to delete the reference lap for the active track and car.
trackMap.referenceLapDeleteSuccess: Reference lap deleted. Recording restarts on the next completed lap.

reset.title: Reset
reset.resetAllDesc: Clears all widget positions, sizes, and preferences. The app will restart automatically.
reset.confirmDescription: Widget layout and all preferences will be lost.

fpsDiagnostics.title: FPS Diagnostics
fpsDiagnostics.description: Measures what the overlay costs the sim, using the sim's own frame rate counter. Run it from a repeatable scene — a replay looping over the same stretch of track with traffic around you.
fpsDiagnostics.detailedDesc: Also measures every enabled widget on its own. Far longer, but names the expensive widget instead of only the expensive configuration.
fpsDiagnostics.switchToSim: Switch to the sim now and leave it focused — it throttles its frame rate in the background, which would make every number meaningless.

error.noWidgets: Enable at least one widget first — there is nothing to measure.
error.noTelemetry: No telemetry from the sim. Start a session and try again.

hud.doneSummary: Full widget set costs {{delta}} FPS. Results in Settings.

telemetryInspector.title: Telemetry inspector
telemetryInspector.description: What the simulator sends and what the app made of it. The two iRacing views are the sim's own data, untouched; the processed views are the app's adapter output. Telemetry refreshes four times a second while this page is open, and costs the app nothing while it is closed.
telemetryInspector.waitingRaw: Waiting for the simulator… A replayed tape holds processed frames only.
telemetryInspector.noteRawTelemetry: Every variable iRacing publishes, under its own names, exactly as kerb reads it from shared memory. Nothing is renamed, masked or rounded. Search also matches the sim's description.
telemetryInspector.noteRawSession: The session YAML exactly as iRacing writes it. The text view is untouched; the tree view only quotes driver and team names first, so they cannot break the parse.
telemetryInspector.noteProcessedTitle: Processed by Marble Trace — not the raw data
telemetryInspector.noteTelemetry: The adapter's output: the kerb frame is mapped into the app's frames in src-tauri/crates/mt-sim-iracing/src/frame_map.rs, and car status fields the car does not declare are blanked there (DeclaredVars). Shown before tiering, demand gating and quantization.
telemetryInspector.noteSession: The parsed session: src-tauri/crates/mt-sim-iracing/src/session_parse.rs picks the fields the app uses and normalizes them; class badges and colors are resolved in car_classes.rs and car_badges.rs.

delivery.title: Delivery counters
delivery.description: How many bundles each recipient actually received, and how many of those carried each demand-gated field. The rate is what the per-window mask work is measured against — a widget's declaration says what was asked for, this says what went on the wire.

developerTools.title: Developer Tools
developerTools.snapshotDesc: Capture current telemetry state and save it next to the settings file.

streamChat.title: Stream chat
streamChat.twitchChannelDesc: Only the name from the channel address: twitch.tv/twitchdev → twitchdev. Read anonymously, no account needed. Leave empty to disable Twitch.
streamChat.youtubeTargetDesc: Any of these works: @MrBeast, youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ, youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ, or just dQw4w9WgXcQ. Given a channel, the current live stream is found automatically.
streamChat.hideCommandsDesc: Drops messages starting with an exclamation mark.
streamChat.ignoredBotsDesc: Comma separated. Their messages never reach the widget.
streamChat.signInDesc: Optional. Unlocks the viewer count and stream uptime in the footer, and replies to chat commands — chat itself works without it.
streamChat.clientIdDesc: This build has no client id, so sign-in needs your own application from dev.twitch.tv/console/apps. Register it as a Public client; no client secret is needed.
streamChat.reconnectDesc: This build needs new Twitch permissions. Reconnect to grant them — chat commands stay unavailable until you do. Reading chat keeps working.

commands.title: Chat commands
commands.enabledDesc: Viewers type a command in your Twitch chat and Marble Trace replies there from your account with data from the current session. Runs on your PC only.
commands.needsSignIn: Sign in to Twitch above: replies are sent from your account.
commands.needsReconnect: Your Twitch sign-in has no permission to post in chat. Reconnect to grant it.
commands.ownChannelOnly: Commands work only in your own channel: the Twitch channel above must be the account you signed in with.
commands.cooldownDesc: How long one command stays quiet after a reply.
commands.globalCooldownDesc: Limits spam: no two replies come closer than this, whichever commands viewers type. Never under 2 seconds, to stay within Twitch limits.

list.gap: Gap to the cars ahead and behind.
list.lap: Current lap and what is left.
list.sof: Strength of field and your iRating.
list.weather: Air and track temperature, wind, track state.
list.lastrace: Track, finish, incidents, SR and iR after your last race. Shows your incidents and rating to everyone.
list.fuel: Fuel state. Rivals watching the stream see your strategy.
list.commands: The list of commands switched on.

streamChat.deviceHint: Enter this code on twitch.tv/activate, then come back — this window updates itself.

errors.clientIdRequired: Fill in the client id first.
errors.sessionExpired: The Twitch session expired. Sign in again.

remote.title: Browser screens
remote.enableDesc: Runs a small web server so a phone or tablet on the same network can open a screen of the active layout in its browser. Devices only watch — they cannot change anything.
remote.portDesc: How often telemetry is sent to the devices — not how often they redraw. 30 per second is smooth for a dashboard and light on Wi-Fi; lap times, fuel and the session clock always arrive in full, whatever this is set to. Change the port only if something else already uses it.
remote.securityDesc: Screen links carry an access token. Regenerate it to lock out every device you have handed a link to.
remote.securityDescOpen: No access token is set, so anyone on this network who knows the address can watch your screens.
remote.tokenDesc: Devices need this token to open a screen. It is already part of the links and QR codes below.
remote.screensDesc: Open the address on the device. Adding it to the home screen hides the browser bar, so the layout gets the whole display.
remote.screensEmpty: No browser screens yet. Add one in the layout editor, next to the monitors.
remote.obsHint: Add this address in OBS as a Browser Source sized {{width}}×{{height}}. Set the screen background to transparent to keep only the widgets on air.
remote.deviceReports: Device reports {{width}}×{{height}} of usable page, on a {{screenWidth}}×{{screenHeight}} display.
remote.addToHomeScreenHint: Add the page to the device home screen to drop the browser bar and get the whole display.
remote.fitToDeviceTooltip: Resize this screen to what the device reports. Widgets keep their place relative to the screen.
remote.lanOffHint: Off: only this computer can open the screens — for capturing a layout as an OBS browser source, or for cutting every device off without taking the setup apart.

companions.addDesc: Detection looks for the sim tools in the folders their installers use. Anything else is added by hand.
companions.listDesc: Started with Marble Trace when they are not already running. Closing the app closes the ones you marked for it, whoever started them — a program that needs administrator rights cannot be closed this way.
companions.notOurs: Started outside Marble Trace — close it where you started it.
companions.removeConfirm: Remove this program from the list?
companions.title: Companion apps

statistics.subtitle: read from the game's telemetry files
statistics.folderMissing: iRacing's telemetry folder was not found. Choose where your .ibt files are.
statistics.reimportDesc: Reads every file in the folder again, the skipped ones too. Sessions whose files are gone stay.
statistics.reimportQueued: Re-import starts when you close the game

bindings.title: Input bindings
bindings.intro: Keys and controller buttons work app-wide, in every layout. Bindings that clash with the sim’s own controls cannot be detected here — check them in iRacing.
bindings.resetConfirm: Reset every binding to its default?
bindings.deviceOffline: Device not connected — the binding is kept.
bindings.captureTitle: Press a key or a device button
bindings.captureHint: Press Escape to cancel. Nothing is saved until you press something.

actions.deltaCycleReference: Cycle the delta reference (PB → PO → SB → SO → SL)
actions.pitServiceToggle: Open the order box away from the pit lane (temporary)
actions.pitServiceAutoMode: Hand this stop to auto mode, or take it back
actions.pitServiceApplyOrder: Order a full stop: calculated fuel and all four tyres (replaces the current order)
actions.pitServiceFuel: Add the calculated amount of fuel
actions.pitServiceFuelPlus: Add one step to the fuel order (step size is set in the widget settings)
actions.pitServiceFuelMinus: Take one step off the fuel order (step size is set in the widget settings)
actions.pitServiceTireCompound: Step to the next tyre compound
actions.pitServicePressurePlus: Raise every tyre's pressure by one step (and order the tyres changed)
actions.pitServicePressureMinus: Lower every tyre's pressure by one step (and order the tyres changed)

bindings.devicesIntro: Wheels, button boxes, joysticks and pedals are detected automatically. A device you have bound something to stays listed while it is unplugged, so its bindings are not lost.
bindings.notInLayoutTooltip: The widget is not in the active layout, so nothing it owns runs — neither its bindings nor its background work, such as automatic pit orders. The show / hide key is the exception: it is what puts the widget back.
bindings.toggleHint: Toggles the box: press again to take it back off the order.

inert.pitServiceAutoMode: Does nothing until Auto fuel or Auto tyres is switched on in the widget settings.

bindings.searchByKeyHint: Press a key or a device button and the list shows what it is bound to.
bindings.searchPressKey: Press a key or a device button…

crewPage.notReady: The engineer needs the engines, a voice and a recognition model — see Overview.

status.title: Status
status.pushToTalkUnbound: Not set — bind one to talk to the engineer

crewPage.packOutdated: The unsaved edits belong to the “{{pack}}” pack, but the crew now speaks “{{language}}”. Save or discard them to open the “{{language}}” pack.

leave.title: Unsaved changes
leave.desc: The crew’s commands have unsaved changes. Save them before you leave?

check.idle: Hold and say a sentence, or type one in the list
check.draftNote: listening for the unsaved changes too
check.voiceOff: The voice is off — turn it on under Overview
check.silence: Nothing heard — check the microphone under Overview
check.unsure: unsure, {{percent}}% — pit orders and question steps will not run

downloads.noCustomVoices: No voices of your own yet
downloads.banner: The voice needs an engine and a voice — about {{size}} MB.
downloads.customVoiceDesc: A Piper .onnx voice with its .onnx.json beside it — one file, or every voice in a folder and the folders under it.
downloads.folderDesc: Downloads, packs and the cache move to the chosen folder as a whole — onto a drive with more room, say. The new folder must be empty; the voice is off while they move.

voice.title: Voice
voice.enabledDesc: Hold push-to-talk (Settings → Bindings) and ask, or give a pit command.
voice.confidenceDesc: A pit command heard less surely than this is not carried out.
voice.testDesc: Hold and speak: shows what was heard and what it would do, without doing it.

phrases.desc: What the engineer says when a sentence is not understood or a value has no data.

commands.tryPlaceholder: Type it as you would say it, e.g. "fuel forty"
commands.unsaidDesc: A sentence may leave the value out: tick "may be left out" on its value block. Then the engineer asks for it, or takes the value chosen here.
commands.sharedAnswers: Out of the car, or when the command fails, the shared answers play — they are at the end of the list.
commands.missingWords: Not in the speech model's vocabulary: {{words}} — a sentence with them is never heard
commands.vocabularyUnchecked: Words are not checked against the speech model: the crew is off, or this language's model is not installed

slots.number: A number from 0 to 200, said in words: "forty", "one twenty". The number words are built in.
slots.tires: Which tyres. For each, the words you call it by; Enter adds a word.
slots.compound: The tyre compound. For each, the words you call it by; Enter adds a word.

mistakes.fileInvalid: Not a pack file — line {{line}}, column {{column}}: {{detail}}
mistakes.numberSlotBuiltIn: Numbers are built in and cannot be redefined
mistakes.noNumberWords: No number words for “{{language}}” — commands with a number are left out
mistakes.emptySlot: Empty braces: a value needs a name
mistakes.tooManySayings: {{count}} ways to say it, at most {{limit}} — fewer choices
mistakes.noValueHere: No value {{name}} here — this phrase has {{offered}}
mistakes.noValueHereNone: No value {{name}} here — this phrase has none
mistakes.carFieldNoTarget: {{field}} is a car's field — this question asks about no car
mistakes.carFieldNoCar: {{field}} is a car's field — there is no car to read it from
mistakes.phraseNeedsSlot: Needs {{slot}} — the car is picked by it
mistakes.phraseOnlySlot: The car is picked by {{slot}} alone, not {{found}}
mistakes.phraseNoSlot: {{found}} — this question does not pick its car by a value
mistakes.macroOutOfRange: A chat macro is 1 to {{limit}}, not {{number}}

pack.title: Pack files
pack.folderDesc: phrases.json and commands.json, with JSON schemas beside them.
pack.shareDesc: The pack's phrases and commands as one archive.
pack.reloadDesc: Read the pack again after editing its files by hand.
pack.switchedOff: Questions that carry out actions came in switched off. Look them over and switch them on yourself:
pack.importFailed: The pack was not imported — yours is unchanged

errors.notAnArchive: The file is not a zip archive.
errors.noPackExport: This language has no pack of your own yet — save an edit first.
errors.noPackImport: The archive holds no voice pack: there is no phrases.json or commands.json in it.

pack.sheetDesc: The commands you can say, with your edits, as a page to print or keep beside the wheel. Opens in the browser; Ctrl+P prints it or saves a PDF.
pack.sheetSaveFirst: Save the changes first: the sheet is made from the saved pack.

questions.title: Your questions
questions.desc: Ask the engineer something of your own, or build a routine: the sentences that call it, what to carry out (pit actions, chat macros) and the answer with values — weather, fuel, position, gaps, laps, time.
questions.name: Name
questions.stepsDesc: In order, before the answer. If one fails, the rest are skipped and the engineer reports it could not be done. Pit actions need you in the car; like a pit command, a routine is not carried out when the sentence was heard unsure.

preview.title: Would say now
preview.desc: The answer from the session the app is connected to: live or a recording. Edits show at once, no need to save; the question's steps are not carried out.
preview.noSession: No session: start iRacing or a recording.
preview.needsCar: Enter the car number or the place the question asks about.
preview.silent: The engineer stays quiet: the pack has no words for this answer.

answers.title: The answer
answers.desc: Said when every field it names has a value.

noCar.title: No such car
noCar.desc: Said when the car is not there: nobody ahead, no car with that number. Left empty, the engineer says there is no data.

noValue.title: No value
noValue.desc: Said when a field the answer names has no value right now (no rain data, no lap yet). Empty: the engineer says there is no data.

fields.desc: Click a field to put it where the cursor is, or type { in an answer.
fields.carNeedsTarget: Pick the car the question asks about to name its fields.

names.name: Driver's name
names.inPit: In the pits: yes or no

values.insertAmount: {{value}} — with its unit, litres or gallons
values.pluralDesc: The word after a number changes: 1 lap, 5 laps. Write the word for each number and the right one is picked.

syntax.title: How to write sentences
syntax.intro: One line stands for many ways of saying it. Only what is written out is recognised, so every way must be in there.

choice.title: (a|b) — one of
choice.desc: Say either word: "fuel forty" or "fill forty".

optional.title: [x] — may be left out
optional.desc: Both "fuel forty" and "fuel forty litres" are recognised.

slot.title: {value} — something named
slot.desc: A number or one of the words listed below goes here; the command gets its value.

nested.title: Nesting
nested.desc: Brackets nest: an optional choice of several words.

replies.title: How to write replies
replies.intro: In the engineer's replies (a|b) and [a] work as in the driver's sentences: the engineer says one of the ways each time. Replies also take fields and number forms — ICU MessageFormat, of which only {field} and plural are supported.

field.title: {field} — a value
field.desc: The value of a field from the sheet, in its own format: a lap time, a number. Fuel, temperatures and speed say their unit in the units chosen in the settings: "40 litres" or "11 gallons" — write no unit after them.

plural.title: plural — the word for the number
plural.desc: # is the number itself. The engineer picks the form by the number: "1 incident", "5 incidents".

exact.title: =N — an exact number
exact.desc: Its own text for one number; checked before the forms.

replies.forms: Forms in English: one (1) and other (everything else). Russian: one — 1, 21…; few — 2–4, 22–24…; many — 0, 5–20…; other — fractions. Spanish: one, many and other; Chinese: other only.

fuel.title: Fuel
fuel.desc: Sets the pit order to the fuel you name, in litres or gallons as chosen in the settings.

fuelToFinish.title: Fuel to the finish
fuelToFinish.desc: Sets the fuel the race still needs.

clearFuel.title: No fuel
clearFuel.desc: Takes fuel out of the pit order.

tires.title: Change tyres
tires.desc: Marks the tyres you name for a change: all, front, rear, left, right or one corner.

clearTires.title: No tyres
clearTires.desc: Takes the tyre change out of the pit order.

compound.title: Tyre compound
compound.desc: Picks the compound, if this session has it.

fastRepair.title: Fast repair
fastRepair.desc: Turns fast repair on in the pit order.

applyPlanned.title: Planned stop
applyPlanned.desc: Sets the fuel the race needs and four tyres.

fuel.title: Fuel left
fuel.desc: The engineer reads the litres in the tank and the laps they last.

gapAhead.title: Gap ahead
gapAhead.desc: Seconds to the car ahead in your class.

gapBehind.title: Gap behind
gapBehind.desc: Seconds to the car behind in your class.

whoAhead.title: Who is ahead
whoAhead.desc: The nearest car ahead on track, any class: number, driver, class in a multiclass race, gap, and whether it is lapped or racing you.

whoBehind.title: Who is behind
whoBehind.desc: The nearest car behind on track, any class: number, driver, class in a multiclass race, gap, and whether it is lapped or racing you.

lapsLeft.title: Laps left
lapsLeft.desc: Laps to the finish, or minutes in a timed race.

pitOrder.title: Pit order
pitOrder.desc: The engineer reads the current pit order.

weather.title: Weather
weather.desc: Air and track temperature, and how hard it rains when it does.

carPosition.title: Car position
carPosition.desc: Where the car with this number runs in its class.

carLastLap.title: Car last lap
carLastLap.desc: The last lap of the car with this number.

carBestLap.title: Car best lap
carBestLap.desc: The best lap of the car with this number.

repeat.title: Repeat
repeat.desc: The engineer says the last line again.

macro.title: Chat macro
macro.desc: Sends an iRacing chat macro by its number (1–15); the macro's text is set in iRacing's options.

answer.carNoLapTime: When the car has no lap time yet
answer.noSuchCar: When there is no such number

ask.fuel: When the value is not said
ask.tires: When the value is not said
ask.compound: When the value is not said
ask.car: When the value is not said

engineer.notInCar: A pit command while out of the car
engineer.cannot: The command could not be carried out

blocks.modeDesc: Blocks put a sentence together from words, choices and values, no marks to type. A sentence whose brackets do not pair up opens as text.
blocks.emptySentence: Type a sentence — Enter or a click away makes the blocks
blocks.emptyReply: Type a reply — Enter or a click away makes the blocks
blocks.choiceHint: Enter adds an option. A single option becomes a plain word.

cheatSheet.title: Voice commands
cheatSheet.legend: a / b — say one of them; [ ] — may be left out; ‹ › — a value you name.
cheatSheet.numberNote: A number from 0 to {{max}}, said in words: “forty”, “one hundred twenty”.
cheatSheet.carNumberNote: A car number is said the way it is painted: “thirty three”, “zero seven”, “five hundred twelve”. Only the cars in the session are heard.

homePage.title: Home
homePage.emptyText: Each time you get in the car, iRacing writes a telemetry file to DocumentsiRacing	elemetry. Marble Trace reads these files while the game is closed and turns them into your sessions, laps, incidents and iRating.
homePage.emptyKept: What it reads is kept, even after you delete the files.

import.paused: Import paused — you are in the game

lastRace.title: Last race
lastRace.iratingUnknown: Shows after your next session in this category

autolog.title: iRacing does not save telemetry files
autolog.text: Statistics come from the files iRacing writes each time you get in the car, and that is switched off in its app.ini. Marble Trace can switch it on for you.
